advisory.finding: The regression test only exercises the escalation case where cfg.model ('low') is an EXACT member of the monkeypatched ladder ['low','high'], so it never covers the production-shaped case where the model is a full identifier not exactly present in the bare-name ladder — the scenario where escalation/model-reporting can silently fail.
merged_from: The split branch (len(bin_) > 1) added/modified by this diff is untested: the new test constructs a single-block bin (comment: 'no split') so the attempt-preservation-on-split semantics and per-sub-bin producing-model recording never execute. A regression that incremented `attempt` on a split (treating a subdivision as a model retry) or mis-recorded the sub-bin model would not be caught.

The per-id design of the `produced` dict (its purpose is that different prerequisite_ids in one run can report DIFFERENT producing models/attempts) is not exercised: the test has exactly one block/id, so cross-id divergence and any id-keying bug (e.g. last-writer-wins leakage across ids) cannot be caught.

The fix's stated goal is to report the escalated model; if escalation never advances in production, the reported model still equals cfg.model, undermining the fix's premise.
dropped.finding: The escalation path uses exact membership `model in ladder` (prerequisites.py:242) to pick the next rung, but the ladder returned by models_at_or_above contains bare names matched by substring (`n in model`, sizing.py:286). With a real full model identifier, `model in ladder` is False, so the code falls to `ladder[0]` and re-runs the SAME first rung with attempt+1 rather than advancing — no real escalation, and attempt grows without terminating on that path.
